newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to restructure Yankee bond arrangers-cbank.
newsitem.headline: Manila to restructure Yankee bond arrangers-cbank.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank may restructure its Yankee bond underwriting team after members gave conflicting advice on the timing and pricing of its long-delayed inaugural float, a Central Bank official said on Thursday.
A meeting to discuss the move was set earlier in the day between Central Bank officials and the underwriting team led by Salomon Brothers, but no details of the outcome were available.
Representatives from the investment houses involved were also not available to comment. Co-lead managers are JP Morgan, Citicorp, Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley and ING Barings.

The Philippines decided to postpone the launch of its $1.25 billion Yankee bond, intended as a benchmark issue, hours before the formal launching last April due to poor U.S. market conditions. President Fidel Ramos said last month the bond could be launched sooner rather than later.
The Central Bank had planned to sell Yankee bonds in tranches of 30 and 100 years.
